description: A department manager must choose a fair response to an employee's recent missed client handoffs and finalize the employee's work boundary, escalation access, coaching plan, and review timing.

shared_context.S1: Jules missed two client handoffs during the past month, and both incidents were recorded in the team's issue log.
shared_context.S2: Jules's current role includes responding to client escalations and completing the related handoff documentation.
shared_context.S3: Mara has authority to choose the formal response and set temporary role boundaries and coaching requirements.
shared_context.S4: The department's normal review routine is for the manager, the employee, and a peer reviewer to give input before a response plan is finalized.

PF1.text: Jules has an approved caregiving arrangement that requires ending work at exactly 16:30 each day; the arrangement was approved by HR this week, but Jules has not yet raised it with Mara because the schedule update is still being processed.

PF2.text: Tessa directly observed five handoffs in which Jules missed the required ownership confirmation, and the department's remediation standard for that pattern is exactly four paired shadowing sessions followed by a review exactly 14 days after the plan begins; Tessa has not put these observations into the formal issue log.

acceptance_conditions: The response must be a developmental reset rather than a formal warning.
Jules's workday must end at exactly 16:30.
Jules must temporarily lose client-escalation access.
The plan must include exactly four paired shadowing sessions.
The review must occur exactly 14 days after the plan begins.
A commitment to document and acknowledge Jules's adjusted schedule must exist.
Tessa's observation pattern must be cited as a basis for the response plan.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'schedule_acknowledgment' and c['target'] == 'Jules' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: The approved caregiving arrangement changes Jules's workday end to exactly 16:30 and requires a schedule-acknowledgment commitment.

The five observed ownership-confirmation gaps change the response to a developmental reset, suspend escalation access, require exactly four paired shadowing sessions, and fix the review at exactly 14 days.
